beats_summary.narration: In twenty twenty-six, Artemis astronauts step onto the permanent shadow of the lunar South Pole on a vital hydration hunt.
beats_summary.speaker: Narrator

beats_summary.narration: From that astronauts, buried beneath meters of dry regolith lies ancient water ice, hidden from sunlight for billions of frozen years.
beats_summary.speaker: Narrator

beats_summary.narration: To find these frozen deposits, crews rely on handheld neutron spectrometers rather than traditional heavy drilling rigs.
beats_summary.speaker: Narrator

beats_summary.narration: From that spectrometers, high-energy cosmic rays bombard the Moon, causing subsurface hydrogen atoms to scatter neutrons with distinct signature speeds.
beats_summary.speaker: Narrator

beats_summary.narration: The spectrometer detects slowed neutrons leaking back up, instantly mapping the invisible moisture hiding in the dark.
beats_summary.speaker: Narrator

beats_summary.narration: From that spectrometer, this real-time chemical plume detection lets astronauts pinpoint exact excavation sites without wasting precious battery life.
beats_summary.speaker: Narrator

beats_summary.narration: Mapping this polar water ice transforms the Moon into a sustainable fueling station for deep space exploration.
beats_summary.speaker: Narrator

beats_summary.narration: From that exploration, neutron spectrometers are the key to unlocking humanity's permanent footsteps across the solar system.
